newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus no comment on Northwest deal report.
newsitem.headline: Airbus no comment on Northwest deal report.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie has "no comment at all" on a newspaper report that Northwest Airlines has tentatively ordered up to 40 A-330 aircraft, an Airbus spokesman said on Tuesday.

The spokesman was responding to a query from Reuters on a report in the electronic edition of the Wall Street Journal, which said there was a tentative order for 40 planes and that half of the aircraft covered by the deal were firm orders.
Asked if he could confirm that there were talks, the Airbus spokesman replied: "We can confirm we are talking with Northwest, as with all our client airlines".

The newspaper cited people familiar with the situation as its sources. It said the order could be worth up to $4.2 billion and amount to the single largest deal yet for widebody aircraft in North America.
Airbus is a consortium comprising state-owned Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Spanish Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA).
